newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CLP to drop Westinghouse turbines.
newsitem.headline: CLP to drop Westinghouse turbines.

text.p: China Light & Power Co Ltd (CLP) said on Friday it would use Chinese generators for a mainland power plant, instead of Westinghouse Electric Corp equipment.
After trying to arrange U.S. Export-Import Bank (Exim) financing for generation equipment for its Shandong power project, CLP was now planning to use Chinese turbines, it said.
"The generator units will come from China," CLP managing director Ross Sayers told a news briefing.
Sayers said there were three potential suppliers for the equipment from China.
CLP executives said they had previously been discussing a deal with Exim using Westinghouse machinery.
"We are no longer negotiating with the U.S. Exim Bank," CLP general manager, finance, Peter Tse said, adding that the potential mainland suppliers all had foreign partners.
The company said it was now talking to the U.K. Export Credits Guarantee Department (ECGD) about using British-assembled boilers supplied by Mitsui Babcock Energy Ltd.
CLP has just over 29 percent in the Shandong project to build generation capacity of 3,600 megawatts in four plants.
